ROUTE R3 -- THE DETERMINIZATION-FREE PROGRESS-MEASURE DESIGN. PAPER RESEARCH ONLY, FILE SCOPE: none, no Lean. Filed on the exact terms the completeness-line reopen decision record sets for this route (specs/archive/926_lean_completeness_line_reopen_decision_record/reports/01_completeness-line-reopen-ruling.md, the Reopening Terms table's R3 row and its recommendation 3), modeled on 879's P9 and on 901's own paper-only posture.

THE QUESTION. Does a determinization-free progress-measure argument for T3 (L-plus ZTime completeness of TM-plus + LC_n + mirror) exist, and what would it need? Deliverable is a VERDICT plus grounds and, on a positive verdict, a DESIGN -- never a theorem and never a Lean declaration.

WHY THIS ROUTE AND NOT THE OTHERS. The determinization obstruction (O1) is `Muller.toRabin_exists`, a `proof_wanted` at Cslib/Computability/Automata/DA/Conversions.lean:112 in the local CSLib fork, whose named consumer is the ban/lull mechanism. R1 -- proving it -- is KEEP CLOSED in this repository, and specifically on the CSLib `require` clause rather than on Recommendation 8's engine-content clause, because a general automata lemma is not sections 7-15 content. "File no task against R1 in this repository" is that record's recommendation 1. A determinization-free progress measure needs no Rabin determinization at all, so it is the one reopened route that bears on the completeness theorem itself while standing clear of both standing rulings.

WHAT A POSITIVE RESULT DOES NOT BUY, STATED UP FRONT. A positive design result does NOT authorize a Lean filing of the design, and this must be written into the report's own framing rather than discovered at its end. The engine-content clause is aimed at the RESULT, not at the lemmas used to reach it: a different construction reaching the same completeness result still trips it. Any Lean filing of whatever this task designs requires a separate, explicit Recommendation 8 reversal by the user, win or lose on the paper design.

DO NOT RE-DERIVE OR RE-MEASURE. (1) The determinization costing is settled: the construction of record is the APPEARANCE-RECORD (LAR) route, Thomas 1997 section 6.1 Theorem 6.5 with Remark 6.6 -- not Safra's and not Piterman's -- on the ground that the lemma's input `a : Muller State Symbol` is ALREADY deterministic, so no determinization construction is removing nondeterminism; the archived Safra/Piterman attribution is a misattribution as to this lemma, accurate only about the composite NBA-to-DRA step. Costed at roughly 1,000 lines over 4-7 phases. If a figure is ever needed, re-cost against those rather than re-measuring from scratch. (2) The acceptance-condition split is settled: a deterministic Muller automaton suffices for the Auxiliary-Atoms rule, which carries no acceptance condition, and does NOT suffice for the ban/lull mechanism, whose banned list is indexed by the automaton's accepting pairs and does not present as a Muller family without a walk-dependent choice only an LAR can make. (3) The architecture of record for the two-sided engine, including the level split, the eliminated cross-certification clauses, the chronicle seed lemma and the four-link Step 3-prime, is already written as a paper proof and is read, not re-derived.

WHERE THE PROGRESS MEASURE WOULD HAVE TO BITE. The ban/lull mechanism is the sole named consumer of the pair-indexed acceptance condition, so it is the component a progress measure must replace. Address, at minimum: what well-founded quantity decreases along a chronicle in place of the banned list; whether it can be read from the hue/type data the alphabet already carries, or demands new syntax the Auxiliary-Atoms rule's freshness side condition would have to admit; whether it survives the two-sidedness, where forward badness is prefix-invariant and backward badness is not; and whether the clock rule's canonical cut still supplies the anchor the level split relies on.

PROHIBITIONS, RULING-LEVEL AND NOT PREFERENCES. (a) NO Lean file is written, edited or filed, under any outcome. Sections 7-15 of the Reynolds engine -- the two-sided chronicle, ban preservation, lulls and hue scheduling, universal non-acceptance, the two-sided truth lemma, the final-frame assembly -- stay barred from any Lean filing under every reopened route, this one included. (b) NO `require` of CSLib in either form; no lakefile.toml edit, no lake-manifest.json edit; the `require` question is not re-opened on this route's account. (c) NO task is filed against R1, and no attempt is made on `Muller.toRabin_exists`, in this repository. (d) NO edit, commit or push in the CSLib fork at /home/benjamin/Projects/cslib. (e) NO upstream PR. (f) Do NOT amend specs/ROADMAP.md's existing Recommendation 8 sentence: the reopen record's recommendation 5 rules explicitly that no amendment is needed, because that sentence's truth is unchanged -- the ruling settles only which parts of each route are reachable without reversing it. (g) The assessment of why the chronicle quotient's OWN Saturation is doubtful -- countably infinite slices, the quotient is not an oriented forest -- is CORRECT and LOAD-BEARING, the reason the universal-cover route exists at all; it is read as a premise, not revisited. (h) No completeness claim lands from this task.

CONFLICT AVOIDANCE, STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN NEGOTIATED. FILE SCOPE is none: this task writes its own specs/ artifacts and touches nothing under FormalSystem/, Tests/, docs/, typst/ or any shared library file, so it collides with no live task's territory by construction -- not with the ladder-realization line, not with the final-frame tasks carrying R2, not with the algebraic chain. It also files nothing, so it cannot contend for a task number or a ruling with any sibling.

CONTINGENCY. A negative verdict is a COMPLETE outcome, not a failure: if no determinization-free progress measure is available, or one is available only at a cost exceeding the LAR route's own, record that with its grounds and with what the obstruction actually is. Either verdict leaves the CSLib `require` decision and Recommendation 8 exactly where they stand; neither is reversed, weakened or re-opened by this task's result.

OPTIONAL, FILED NOT SCHEDULED -- AND LOAD-BEARING AS A CHECK. This task stays unscheduled: status HOLD (user ruling 2026-10-03; prior_status not_started), dependencies [], nothing depends on it. What has changed since it was filed is the claim that "none of the L-plus programme's recommendations rest on it." That is no longer accurate. Its 2EXPTIME lower bound -- ARGUED, not formalized -- is the sanity ceiling that three live records cite against any proposed decision procedure for L-plus. It is load-bearing as a check even while unproved.

ITS ROLE: THE SANITY CEILING. Three records USE this task's argued lower bound as the bound-sanity check -- nothing cheaper than 2EXPTIME is a credible decision procedure. All three were re-verified against the tree on 2026-10-07 (task 738), at their archive locations:

1. specs/archive/718_omega_sequence_decidability_full_lplus/reports/02_ranked-route-analysis.md (archived), the "Complexity sanity check" bullet at line 258: "the CTL* 2EXPTIME-hardness reduction (filed, argued in both directions) is the lower bound; determinization-based upper bounds are doubly exponential, which is consistent. Any proposal cheaper than 2EXPTIME is prima facie wrong. No bound committed."

2. Task 719's description (ray layer, seam gluing and stab fibre; completed and archived at specs/archive/719_ray_layer_seam_gluing_and_stab_fibre, record in specs/archive/state.json -- now provenance rather than a live document), Deliverable 5: "DO NOT LAND A COMPLEXITY CLAIM; the CTL-star 2EXPTIME lower bound is the sanity check on any proposed bound."

3. specs/archive/721_decidability_programme_review_l_and_lplus/reports/01_decidability-programme-review.md (archived) section 3.1 (L-plus routes forward), line 147 -- its Section C ruling on this task is at line 183: "the CTL* 2EXPTIME-hardness argument (task 713, ARGUED) is the lower bound on any proposed procedure; nothing cheaper is credible; no bound is committed here."

ARGUED, NOT FORMALIZED -- AND EVERY CITING RECORD MUST SAY SO. The bound is an argument in prose, not a machine-checked theorem. No Lean declaration establishes it; there is no CTL-star syntax or semantics in the tree to state it against. Every record that cites it must describe it that way, with the ARGUED qualifier attached, exactly as the three records above do. A citation that presents the bound as established, or that drops the qualifier, is a defect in that record.

NO UPPER-BOUND CLAIM MAY LAND FROM THIS TASK. The programme commits to no complexity bound. This task's content is a LOWER bound used as a ceiling: it rules proposals out, it never certifies that any procedure achieves a cost. Deriving or landing an upper-bound claim from it -- in this task's artifacts, in a citing record, or in the write-up -- is a defect, not a result. The asymmetry is the point: a lower bound says "nothing cheaper is credible", it does not say "this much suffices."

GOAL. Raise the 2EXPTIME-hardness of L-plus Z-time validity from ARGUED to MACHINE-CHECKED. The argument is given in both directions in specs/archive/706_lplus_finite_model_property_and_completeness/reports/01_lplus-finite-model-property-research.md section Q4 ("The true order of the state bound"), completing what task 703's round-2 report argued in one direction only -- now archived at specs/archive/703_lplus_compression_and_completeness/reports/02_semantics-first-compression-research.md section 1.6 ("The complexity picture").

THE REDUCTION. Translate CTL-star by A |-> stab and X |-> bottom U ., with non-strict U rendered as e or (g and (g U e)). FORWARD: a rooted total Kripke structure becomes bi-serial by adding one fresh state with a self-loop and an edge to the root, which leaves forward paths from the original states unchanged; stab at (sigma, t) with sigma t = w ranges over histories through w, whose futures are exactly the forward paths from w, and the translation is pure-future so its truth depends only on the future (truth_congr_agreeFrom). BACKWARD: from a Z-model of the translation at (sigma, t), the Kripke structure of the state graph forward-reachable from sigma t satisfies the CTL-star formula at sigma t, by the same two facts read backwards. CTL-star satisfiability is over arbitrary, possibly infinite structures, so no finiteness is needed anywhere.

WHAT IT WOULD BUY. Formalization would turn the ceiling from an argued check into a theorem-backed one: the sharpest available limit on how good ANY certificate class can be. As task 706's Q4 and the archived 703 round-2 section 1.6 record the consequence, with the reduction a theorem no complete certificate class with singly exponential, polynomially checkable certificates could exist for full L-plus without a complexity-theoretic surprise.

CANONICAL WORDING OF THE CONSEQUENCE (quote this, verbatim, in any record that repeats it). L-plus Z-time validity -- equivalently, by negation, L-plus Z-time satisfiability -- is 2EXPTIME-hard by the CTL-star reduction. ARGUED, NOT FORMALIZED: no Lean declaration establishes it. CONSEQUENCE, stated for NON-VALIDITY: if every non-valid formula had a certificate of size singly exponential in the closure size, checkable in time polynomial in the certificate's size, then non-validity (satisfiability of the negation) would be in NEXPTIME and, equivalently, validity would be in co-NEXPTIME; hence 2EXPTIME would be contained in NEXPTIME, equivalently in co-NEXPTIME, since 2EXPTIME is closed under complement. That containment is not refuted but is widely disbelieved. The two class names are the same statement read from opposite sides of the complement: a record may name either, but must say which problem it is placing (NON-VALIDITY with NEXPTIME; VALIDITY with co-NEXPTIME). This is a LOWER bound used as a ceiling: nothing cheaper than 2EXPTIME is credible. It says nothing about any cost sufficing for L-plus and must never be restated as an upper bound. Sources: 706 Q4 (validity / co-NEXPTIME reading) and 703 round-2 section 1.6 (satisfiability / NEXPTIME reading), reconciled 2026-10-07 (task 738): the apparent divergence was one of presentation, not content.

WHAT IT COSTS. A CTL-star syntax and semantics must be added to the tree, which is substantial standalone work the programme otherwise has no need for. Task 706 rates the risk that the reduction has a gap as LOW (its R4) and records it as affecting the complexity picture only.

KEEP-OR-ABANDON IS A PHASE 0 USER RULING, NOT MADE HERE. This revision records the task's role; it does not decide the task's fate and does not schedule it. The decidability-programme review's Section C (specs/archive/721_decidability_programme_review_l_and_lplus/followup-scope-spec.md, Section C at line 220) restates the choice as the user's: keep this as a write-up note, or abandon it. If the ruling is to abandon, the three citing records need their sanity-check bullets re-sourced to the argument's actual homes (706's Q4 and the archived 703 round-2 section 1.6) rather than to this task.

roadmap_batches.description: Restore the dataset readers the c7 zstd compression broke; the only runnable hygiene line
roadmap_batches.rationale:
FIRST on the instruction to attend to repository hygiene before the proof-mode programme, and now the ONLY item on this list that is both genuinely clean-up and dispatchable at all. The test-coverage line that led this list when the pass began -- three `FormalSystem/` module groups with zero referencing tests anywhere under `Tests/` -- reached `completed` MID-PASS, in the concurrent session that held it, so it is retired from this list rather than reordered within it; that is also why nothing now precedes this line.

Raised out of the examples/zstd pair it used to share a line with, because that pairing called it an additive format capability and its own record says something stronger: `data/bmlogic-c7.jsonl` was compressed to `data/bmlogic-c7.jsonl.zst` (17G -> 153M, lossless, sha256 of the decompressed stream verified identical), and CONSUMERS THAT HARDCODE THE UNCOMPRESSED PATH ARE CURRENTLY BROKEN. A repository with broken readers is the most literal hygiene finding available here, and unlike every other hygiene candidate it has no unmet predecessor: both its edges (631, 632) are archived and it sits in wave 1.

Research-first by its own record: inventory every reader and writer of `.jsonl` datasets before changing any of them -- the Python validators and curators, the shell runners, the Lean executables, and the `path` fields in `data/*_metadata.json` -- then choose one shared `open_dataset()` helper handling both `.jsonl` and `.jsonl.zst` (and how that dependency is provided), and decide how the Lean executables reach compressed data given that Lean has no native zstd. Plain `.jsonl` must keep working, and every updated consumer is verified against the compressed file.

Two stale-path traps annotated in its own description, worth re-deriving rather than trusting: `migrate_schema_v2.py` and `standardize_metadata.py` were DELETED by an archived predecessor, so drop them from the inventory step; and the Lean executables it names as `FormalSystem/Automation/*Main.lean` are now `BimodalTools/*Main.lean` with tests under `Tests/BimodalToolsTest/`, built by `lake build BimodalTools` rather than a default `lake build`.

Alone on its line because it declares no `file_scope` of its own, so an implementation co-dispatch reaches it only through the `absent_file_scope` gate, which admits the lowest-numbered absent-scope candidate per cycle. Its reconciliation with 257 (the externally blocked Hugging Face migration) is a design question this task ANSWERS, not an edge: both reach `data/README.md`, 257 cannot run until a credential exists, and nothing here waits on it.

roadmap_batches.description: De-contend the shared files, then run the four pre-gate streams up to 947's GO / RE-PLAN gate
roadmap_batches.rationale:
THE PROOF-MODE PROGRAMME STARTS HERE, and this line still STOPS AT 947 because 947 is a gate, not a milestone -- unchanged from the previous ordering and re-confirmed against `records/proof-mode.md`'s Gates section. GO requires the proof-mode scripts to be shorter in aggregate and for a clear majority of declarations, with no declaration needing a raw term-mode escape longer than its original; otherwise the verdict is RE-PLAN, the report recommends how each later record should change, and the work stops for user review so that nothing downstream is dispatched on an unrevised plan. Batching anything after 947 into this line would be scheduling exactly the work the gate exists to be able to cancel.

Eight members, which is exactly `MAX_TASKS`, and the line is FULLY DEPENDENCY-INCLUSIVE: every member's declared predecessors are either in this batch or already terminal (955's other edge, 958, completed -- which is also why `modal_search` is functional again rather than hard-failing on every bimodal goal). 960 heads it alone by its own edges: M0 splits the acceptance tests into one file per tactic family under `Tests/BimodalTest/Automation/ProofMode/` and sections the usage guide per family, with the 31 existing examples passing unchanged. That split is what lets the rest of this line run at once instead of queueing behind one test file, so it is first on measurement, not on taste.

Out of 960 run four independent streams, which the intra-batch edges sequence into five waves (960; then 944, 955, 961, 954; then 945; then 946; then 947). (1) The bimodal scope core 944 -> 945 -> 946, each extending the scope rules the one before adds. 944 makes a box scope S5-aware, carrying `box A` and `diamond A` into the body -- note the axiom `modal_5_collapse` is `diamond box A -> box A`, NOT 5, so `diamond A -> box diamond A` must be derived -- with STRIPPING kept as the default so existing scripts keep their meaning. 945 lets box hypotheses cross into G and H scopes by MF and derived TF, used nowhere in the proof mode today. 946 adds the always/sometimes scope rules plus the P1-P6 acceptance scripts, and carries its own trap: `sometimes` is DEFINED as a negation, not a disjunction, so operator matching will see a negation and the `P or phi or F phi` form must be proved as a pure rule first. (2) 955, the leaf closer: `propDecide`, reflective and kernel-`decide`-only, which must first discharge the goal's object assumptions into implications because it proves closed theorems and weakens; `modal_search` is admissible ONLY as a bounded fallback for single-modality leaves, never as the default, and `native_decide` is forbidden. It uses no scope rule, so it runs beside the bimodal stream. (3) 961, the trust and cost baseline: an axiom-set assertion per tactic family in TM and TM-plus on the pattern of `Tests/BimodalTest/WalkthroughAxioms.lean`, plus a recorded derivation-size and elaboration-time baseline with the command that reproduces it. Its edge into 947 is sequencing-only and exists so the gate report can QUOTE a cost figure rather than assert one. (4) 954, error-message coverage: a `#guard_msgs` negative test for every `throwError` site in `FormalSystem/Automation/ProofMode/`, or a listing as unreachable with a reason, plus a check that fails when a site is added without a test. It is in this line and not after the gate deliberately -- it tests the tactics as merged and changes no rule, so it does not wait on the verdict, and once its check is in, every later record covers its own error sites as it adds them.

Two integrity constraints run through the whole line and are what keep the gate from being self-confirming: no pure rule may restate one of P1-P6 or exist only to make one of them a one-liner, and no script may cite anything in `FormalSystem/Theorems/Perpetuity/`. That second constraint is also why 944 and 945 are forbidden from importing it -- `modal5`, `boxToPast` and friends are precisely the lemmas 947 re-proves. `Theorems/` must not import `Automation/`, and every tactic must assemble native `DerivationTree`/`PlusDerivationTree` constructors and proved rules only; nothing semantic may stand in for a derivation.

SCHEDULING, measured and now different from what this list used to say: every member declares a `file_scope`, so the `absent_file_scope` serialization no longer applies to this line at all. What remains is ordinary scope overlap on the shared files `records/proof-mode.md` names -- the aggregators `Tests/BimodalTest/Automation/ProofModeTest.lean`, `FormalSystem/Automation/ProofMode.lean` and `FormalSystem/Theorems/ProofMode.lean`, the guide index `docs/user-guide/derivation-proof-mode.md`, and the two ProofMode READMEs -- each edited one line at a time, which SERIALIZES implementation without ordering it. 960 declares `Tests/BimodalTest/Automation/ProofMode/` and `docs/user-guide/proof-mode/` at directory granularity because it creates that layout, so it contends with every member below it and must land first in practice as well as in the graph. Research and planning are not serialized. Re-run the line until every member reports terminal.

roadmap_batches.description: Deduction theorems for Star and Open: no predecessors, off the gate, Open half demoted
roadmap_batches.rationale:
ON ITS OWN LINE BECAUSE IT SITS OUTSIDE THE PROGRAMME'S SPINE ENTIRELY. 962 is M9b: a proved deduction theorem, generalized K and context substitution for each of the Star and Open calculi, OR a written reason why it cannot be had. It carries NO predecessor -- it is metatheory about two calculi and needs no interface, no scope rule and no gate verdict -- and nothing depends on it except 953, whose language accounting cites either its theorem or its written obstruction. It is in wave 1 of the live graph alongside 960.

It is placed here rather than raised above the pre-gate line for one reason stated plainly: its OPEN half falls under the standing 2026-11-05 ruling that places the L-triangle line behind L-plus critical-path work, so it is kept and visible but not dispatched ahead of the rule set the gate measures. Its Star half carries no such demotion and could be taken at any time.

It collides with nothing. Its `file_scope` is `FormalSystem/StarLanguage/StarDeduction.lean`, `FormalSystem/OpenLanguage/OpenDeduction.lean`, the two language aggregators and their READMEs -- no ProofMode file, no test aggregator, no guide index -- so it can run beside any other line on this list, including the pre-gate line above. Note the live overlap with 876, which declares `FormalSystem/OpenLanguage/` at directory granularity: that serializes the two, it does not order them, and no edge is warranted in either direction.

Schedule it expecting a WRITTEN REASON as a legitimate terminal outcome for either calculus. A deduction theorem that cannot be proved for a calculus is a result about that calculus, not a failed task.

roadmap_batches.description: The linear-time rules and gate two's measured report; enterable only on a GO verdict at 947
roadmap_batches.rationale:
ENTERABLE ONLY ON A GO VERDICT AT 947, which is why this is a separate line rather than the tail of the one above. 949's own record instructs it to read `docs/development/proof-mode-adequacy-perpetuity.md` FIRST and, if the verdict is RE-PLAN, to stop and report instead of implementing. On RE-PLAN the correct next action is `/revise` against the gate's per-record recommendations, not this line.

The three members are the chain 949 -> 950 -> 948 and they are the temporal half of the rule set whose perpetuity half the pre-gate line reached. 949 opens TL's and CN's three ordered cases from two eventualities or two Until/Since facts, and must PERMUTE `tempLinearity`'s disjuncts into CN's order (together, first earlier, second earlier) rather than exposing TL's own different order to the user. 950 adds Until/Since introduction, one-step ZTime unfolding -- lifted along a `ZTime <= fc` certificate the way `lstep` does, because the unfolding theorems are stated at the fixed class with no `...At` variant -- and the induction rule of which the existing `forwardInvariantRule` is the special case. Whether the linearity case split is actually NEEDED for that induction rule is an OPEN DECISION in `records/proof-mode.md`: introduction and unfolding provably do not need it (`left_mono_until_G`, `unfoldForward`, `unfoldBackward`, `unfoldBackwardSince` take no linearity premise), and the question is settled the moment 950's plan states the induction rule's formula. State the formula before proving anything.

948 is GATE TWO, and it has NO VERDICT as filed -- a point this list previously left implicit. Its output is a measured report plus a missing-rule list, each item either added there or named with a proposed follow-up description; 952, 956 and 968 each take the rule set after it as their input. The slice is fixed IN ADVANCE so it cannot be chosen for ease: at least four declarations from each of `FormalSystem/Theorems/TemporalDerived.lean`, `ConnectDerived.lean` and `LinearityDerived.lean`, including `tempLinearity`, with the chosen list stated in the plan and no script citing the declaration it re-proves. Do not let the missing-rule list land without a declared consumer for each item.

The 178 adjacency is now VISIBLE to the admission check rather than invisible: 948 declares `FormalSystem/Examples/ProofMode/Temporal.lean`, under the `FormalSystem/Examples/` directory 178 declares at directory granularity (as 947 does with `.../Perpetuity.lean`). That is shared territory with NEITHER record presupposing the other, so no edge was filed and none is warranted; it serializes the two lines against each other and nothing more.

roadmap_batches.description: Frame coverage at Dense and RTime, held by the gate but needing nothing else from it
roadmap_batches.rationale:
ALONE, AND INTERLEAVABLE WITH THE LINE ABOVE. M7 has NO hard dependency: `density` takes `Dense <= fc`, `coDerived` takes `RTime <= fc`, `prior_U_gap` and `sep` are axiom constructors at RTime, and the certificate pattern is the one `lstep` already has. Its only edge, onto 947, is SEQUENCING-ONLY and was filed for a single reason -- so that a RE-PLAN verdict can hold a record that adds new tactics. Nothing in its deliverable uses an Until or Since rule from the linear-time line or anything from the usability line, so on a GO verdict it runs beside both.

Its territory confirms that: `FormalSystem/Theorems/ProofMode/{Dense,PlusDense,Real,PlusReal}.lean`, `FormalSystem/Automation/ProofMode/Frame.lean` and `.../ProofMode/FrameTest.lean` are disjoint from 949/950's `Temporal`/`Discrete` files and from 963/964's `Basic`/`Meta`/`Display` files. The overlap is confined to the aggregators and the two READMEs, which serialize rather than order.

Deliverable: DN at Dense, and PU, SEP and CO at RTime, each with a pure rule and a tactic whose frame certificate is SOLVED when reflexive and otherwise surfaced as an ordinary Lean goal, tested at a concrete and at an abstract frame class in TM and TM-plus.

One filed POSITION worth knowing, reversible by changing one edge: 951 runs BEFORE 952, which means its rules are written twice (TM and TM-plus) and 952 then removes the copies. The exchange is an interface designed having seen a Dense and an RTime rule. The alternative -- writing these rules once over the interface -- is a real option, not an oversight, and it is a user call, not this list's.

roadmap_batches.description: The usability stream: nested intro patterns, then the goal display designed against them
roadmap_batches.rationale:
ONE STREAM, TWO RECORDS, STACKED. Neither has a hard dependency -- both work on the elaborators as they stand -- and both are held by gate one for the same reason 951 is: they add tactic behaviour a RE-PLAN verdict could change. 963 additionally carries a 954 edge, which is the one edge in this pair that does real work: the error-coverage check from the pre-gate line is what 963's new error sites must pass, so the check lands before the sites do. 964 then carries 963, stacked in the same stream and designed against the scripts gate one's module actually produces rather than against invented ones.

963 lets `lcases` and `lintro` take nested patterns, with tests and a guide section. 964's deliverable carries the constraint that makes it worth filing separately: a goal view may elide a hypothesis's object context ONLY when it EQUALS the goal's context, and must keep a differing context visibly marked -- a differing context is exactly what makes `lexact`/`lapply` reject a hypothesis inside a new scope, so eliding it would hide the one fact a user needs to debug the rejection.

Territory: 963 declares `Basic.lean`, `Meta.lean`, `BasicTest.lean` and `ErrorTest.lean`; 964 declares `Display.lean`, `DisplayTest.lean` and `docs/user-guide/proof-mode/display.md`. They share only the `FormalSystem/Automation/ProofMode.lean` aggregator, the guide index and the Automation README -- edited one line at a time, which serializes the pair rather than breaking it. Both feed 952, which rewrites every elaborator they touch, so neither may be left open when the join is dispatched.

roadmap_batches.description: Adoption after a GO verdict, pending the user ruling on what default means for the mode
roadmap_batches.rationale:
ALONE, AND BLOCKED ON A RULING NO DISPATCH SUPPLIES. M12's only hard dependency is gate one with a GO verdict -- it carries no rule-set dependency at all, so it opens the moment the verdict lands and is NOT held behind the linear-time, frame or usability work. That is why it is a line of its own and not the tail of any of them.

What it does need first is OPEN DECISION 2 in `records/proof-mode.md`: what "default" means. Three candidates are on the table and they are materially different pieces of work -- new example and case-study modules MUST use the mode; or new derived theorems get a proof-mode companion under `FormalSystem/Examples/`; or the mode stays OPTIONAL and this record only fixes where proof-mode proofs live. The constraint any ruling must respect is the layer order: proofs under `FormalSystem/Theorems/` CANNOT be written in the mode, so "default everywhere" is not among the options. Dispatching this record before the ruling lands means guessing the deliverable.

Its done-when is otherwise concrete: the guide states where proof-mode proofs live and which kinds of new derivation are to be written in the mode, and at least one module OUTSIDE the tests and the two adequacy modules is proved in the mode. Its territory (`docs/user-guide/derivation-proof-mode.md`, `FormalSystem/Examples/ProofMode/Adoption.lean`, `FormalSystem/Examples.lean`, `FormalSystem/Examples/README.md`) overlaps 947 and 948 under `FormalSystem/Examples/` and 178's directory declaration, which serializes it against those lines without ordering it further.

roadmap_batches.description: The join: prove every rule once over one object interface, with nothing else editing ProofMode
roadmap_batches.rationale:
THE JOIN, AND THE SERIALIZATION POINT OF THE WHOLE PROGRAMME. 952 carries one edge from each of the four lines above it -- 948, 951, 963 and 964 -- which is a faithful rendering of what M8 is: the single point where the five streams meet. Today every rule exists once for TM and once for TM-plus (about 620 lines of copies under `FormalSystem/Theorems/ProofMode/Plus*.lean`) with the elaborators dispatching through hard-coded name pairs. 952's record is explicit that a META-LEVEL REGISTRY OF NAME PAIRS DOES NOT SATISFY IT: what is wanted is an OBJECT-LEVEL typeclass over the formula type and its derivation family, packaging assumption, modus ponens, weakening, lift, deduction, cut, context substitution and a generalized K rule per universal operator, with the pure rules proved once over that class and the instance resolved from the goal. Equally explicit: extract the interface from the rule set AS IT STANDS AFTER THE ADEQUACY TESTS -- do not design it ahead of them. That is why it sits below both gates rather than being hoisted up as foundational refactoring, and why language-specific capabilities (the TM-only leaf closer, TM-plus stability scopes) belong in optional members or separate classes, never as exceptions written back into elaborators.

IT IS ALONE ON ITS LINE BY MEASUREMENT, NOT PREFERENCE. 952 is the one proof-mode record that declares BOTH `FormalSystem/Theorems/ProofMode/` and `FormalSystem/Automation/ProofMode/` at DIRECTORY granularity, and it does so on purpose: it rewrites every elaborator and restates every pure rule, so nothing that edits either directory may run beside it. Every other open proof-mode record declares at least one file under one of those two directories. Batching anything with it would be declaring a collision, and placing a later record on the same line would have it wait anyway.

One ruling is better taken before this record than discovered inside it: OPEN DECISION 3, where the Minus instance lives. Its deduction theorem is `FormalSystem/Metalogic/Conservativity/MinusDeduction.lean` at layer 3, so either the instance sits at layer 3 or that module moves down -- and that bears directly on how the interface is laid out here, not only on 953 where it surfaces.

roadmap_batches.description: The Minus instance and the per-language accounting, whose honest outcome may be a written reason
roadmap_batches.rationale:
FIRST OF THE FOUR LINES THE JOIN OPENS. M9a gives the Minus calculus a proof-mode instance with acceptance tests, and accounts for EVERY directory matching `FormalSystem/*Language/` in the guide -- by an instance or by a stated reason. It is the record where the programme says what it does NOT cover, which is why it must not be scheduled as uniformly implementation.

Its two edges are both load-bearing. On 952, because an instance is an instance OF the interface. On 962, because the Star and Open rows of the accounting cite either 962's proved deduction theorem or 962's written obstruction -- that edge is the whole reason 962 sits on its own line early rather than here. Hybrid, Nomic, Quant and Source have no derivation calculus at all and get one line each saying so; Minus already has a deduction theorem and is the expected first instance.

The layer problem is real and is OPEN DECISION 3: `MinusDeduction.lean` lives at layer 3 under `FormalSystem/Metalogic/Conservativity/`, so the instance cannot sit under `FormalSystem/Theorems/` the way the TM and TM-plus rules do -- either it sits at layer 3 or that module moves down. The record declares `FormalSystem/Automation/ProofMode/Instances/` for its own code, which overlaps 952's directory declaration and so stays strictly after it.

Expect a WRITTEN REASON rather than code for at least some languages, and do not expand this record to close a gap it only names: the instruction in its own record is to record the reason in the user guide and propose a follow-up task.

roadmap_batches.description: Verification architecture: the liveness rules, the report that hinges it, and the two closers
roadmap_batches.rationale:
FOUR MEMBERS, TWO KINDS OF DELIVERABLE, AND 957 IS THE HINGE -- which is exactly why 966 and 967 are batched HERE rather than on a line of their own. 967's hard dependency is M11, whose report fixes the division of labour with the ModelChecker, and its sequencing dependency is M14a so that an unclosed leaf is measured against the FULL closer. Splitting 966 -> 967 onto a separate line would name 967 without its out-of-batch blocker 957, which is dead weight by this list's own rule. Batched together, the intra-batch edges sequence cleanly: 956 and 966 open at once, then 957, then 967.
